chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from his forefathers: that ʿAlī عليه السلام did not perform ghusl on ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, may Allah have mercy on him, nor on Hāshim ibn ʿUtbah, who was al-Mirqāl.

He buried them in their blood and did not perform salat over them. So what this report contains, that he did not perform salat over them, is an error from the narrator, because we have already explained the obligation of salat over every deceased person, and this is a matter of consensus among the rightful sect. We have mentioned in the rulings concerning martyrs that wherein there is sufficiency in our larger book.

And it is possible that the manner of it is the relating of what some of the ʿAmmah narrate from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, as though he عليه السلام said: they narrate from ʿAlī عليه السلام that he did not perform salat over them, and that is contrary to the truth, as we have explained.

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الْفِرْقَةِ الْمُحِقَّةِ: the rightful sect, i.e. the true Shia community

ai.seo_question: Is salat over a Muslim martyr obligatory according to al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This passage addresses a report about the burial of two martyrs and rejects the claim that Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام did not perform salat over them. It affirms, in line with Shia scholarly consensus, the legal obligation of salat over every deceased Muslim, including martyrs.
